title: How does the orchestrator role pass from one agent to the next?
context: The orchestrator is a role, not a session. When an agent's context grows large it should retire and a new one take over seamlessly, with the board as the shared memory. The question is when and how the swap happens.

options.name: Retire at a threshold
options.summary: The orchestrator watches its own context; past a set size, or on your word, it writes a handoff memo, closes or reassigns its threads, and the hub starts its successor.

pros: Keeps context between rounds while it is cheap to
One clear moment to check the handoff memo
cons: Anything not yet written to the board is lost if it crashes
Needs a reliable sense of its own context size

options.name: Stateless: new agent every round
options.summary: Every time there is something to handle, the hub starts a fresh orchestrator that reads the board index, acts, writes back and exits.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='110' y='20' width='100' height='40' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='44' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Board</text><line x1='60' y1='110' x2='125' y2='62' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='125,62 121.7,68.2 118.1,63.3' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='190' y1='62' x2='260' y2='110' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='260,110 253.1,108.9 256.5,103.9' fill='currentColor'/><rect x='10' y='112' width='90' height='45' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='55' y='138.5' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Round 1</text><rect x='115' y='112' width='90' height='45' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='138.5' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Round 2</text><rect x='220' y='112' width='90' height='45' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='265' y='138.5' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Round 3</text><line x1='160' y1='62' x2='160' y2='110' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='160,110 157.0,103.7 163.0,103.7' fill='currentColor'/></svg>
pros: Nothing ever lives only in a context, so no handoff can go wrong
Forces the board to be complete
cons: Re-reads the board every round: more tokens and slower
Loses the short-term thread of a busy hour

options.name: Overlap handoff
options.summary: At the threshold, the successor starts, reads the board and memo, and shadows one round; the old orchestrator answers its questions, then retires.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='10' y='40' width='120' height='40' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='70' y='64' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Orchestrator 1</text><rect x='70' y='100' width='120' height='40' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='130' y='124' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Orchestrator 2</text><line x1='110' y1='80' x2='125' y2='98' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='125,98 118.6,95.1 123.3,91.2' fill='currentColor'/><text x='250' y='70' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>one round</text><text x='250' y='86' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>together</text></svg>
pros: Smoothest for you: no gap in the conversation
cons: Two orchestrators at once need a rule for who answers
Costs a round of double work

recommendation: Retiring at a threshold keeps cheap context while it helps and makes the handoff memo the single checkpoint; requiring every decision and requirement to hit the board as it happens covers the crash case.
change_mind: If the board index stays small enough to read every round cheaply, stateless (B) is simpler and safer.
